entries.what: store database and app volume backups on Cloudflare R2
entries.summary: Send Levelrail database dumps and app volume archives to your Cloudflare R2 bucket through its S3 compatible API. It uses the dedicated `r2` provider type.
gets: Scheduled and manual backups of databases and app volumes written to your Cloudflare R2 bucket.
A Test connection button that checks the credential before a 3am backup depends on it.
Retention by count and by age, applied by the control plane after each run.
entries.ui_path: Settings > Backup targets (/settings/backup-targets), then add a target and pick the Cloudflare R2 tile
cli: levelrail-cli backup-targets create --name r2-backups --provider r2 --endpoint https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com --region auto --bucket levelrail-backups --access-key-id <KEY_ID> --secret-access-key <SECRET>
auth: R2 API token credentials: the access key id and secret access key it issues.

permissions.detail: Needed by Test connection, which calls HeadBucket.
Needed to upload each dump or volume archive.
Needed for restore and backup verification.
Needed for retention pruning.

entries.endpoint: Provider type `r2`. Endpoint: `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` (you must supply it). Default region: `auto`.
limits: Test connection proves the bucket exists and answers, not that the key can write or delete.
Every backup write returns 501 until the control plane has a master key configured.

trouble.problem: Test connection says authentication rejected
trouble.fix: The API answered 401 or 403. Re-enter the access key id and secret, and confirm the key is allowed on this bucket.

trouble.problem: Test connection says bucket not found
trouble.fix: The API answered 404. Check the bucket name, the region and the endpoint host together: for R2 the endpoint carries your account id, so a wrong id also looks like a missing bucket.

trouble.problem: A manual backup fails with 507
trouble.fix: The control plane data directory has less free space than APP_MIN_BACKUP_DISK_MB (default 256). Free space there and retry.

faq.q: Can the same Cloudflare R2 bucket hold database and volume backups?
faq.a: Yes. A backup target is its own resource, and any number of databases and app volumes can reference it by id.

faq.q: Will I see the secret key again after saving?
faq.a: No. Credentials are write-only: responses never echo them, and rotating means supplying a new pair with `backup-targets update`.

entries.what: pull private images from Docker Hub
entries.summary: Store a credential for Docker Hub so deploys and image checks can pull private images from it.
gets: Private images from Docker Hub pulled with the stored credential at deploy time.
Test connection, which authenticates the typed credential and stores nothing.
An expiry reminder when you record or derive an expiry date.
entries.ui_path: Settings > Registry credentials (/settings/registry-credentials?connect=dockerhub)
auth: your Docker Hub user as username with a personal access token.

permissions.detail: A read-only token is enough to pull.

entries.endpoint: Registry host: `docker.io`.
limits: The credential holds a username and password or token only; it is not used to push images.

trouble.problem: Test connection reports authentication rejected
trouble.fix: The registry answered unauthorized. Use a Docker Hub personal access token, not the account password, and confirm it is not expired.

trouble.problem: Test connection says the registry could not be reached
trouble.fix: The host did not answer. Check the registry host spelling and that the control plane can reach it outbound.

trouble.problem: A deploy fails pulling an image that exists

entries.what: single sign-on with Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak or any SAML identity provider
entries.summary: Connect one or more SAML 2.0 identity providers, map directory groups to roles and optionally require single sign-on for non-root users.
gets: A sign-in button per enabled connection, with SP initiated login only.
Group to role mappings with priorities, re-applied on each sign-in when sync is on.
Require SSO for non-root users while root keeps password access as break-glass.
entries.ui_path: Settings > Single sign-on (/settings/sso), then Add SAML connection
auth: SAML 2.0 signed responses, validated against the stored IdP certificates. Encrypted assertions are supported.

permissions.detail: Every SSO setting needs a root session or token.
An https dashboard URL must be set; entity ID and ACS URL are built from it, never from the Host header.
The service provider signing key is stored encrypted with it.

entries.endpoint: Entity ID and metadata URL: `https://<dashboard>/api/v1/auth/saml/<id>/metadata`. ACS URL (HTTP-POST binding): `https://<dashboard>/api/v1/auth/saml/<id>/acs`.
limits: Interim hand built implementation, behind the saml-scim beta feature and off by default. While off its routes answer 404.
Sign-in is SP initiated only: IdP initiated responses are refused.
Clock skew tolerance is three minutes and a response must be no older than 90 seconds.

trouble.problem: Response could not be verified
trouble.fix: The IdP certificate rotated (import the metadata again), clocks differ by more than three minutes, or the IdP signs for a different entity ID or ACS URL.

trouble.problem: Account has not been set up
trouble.fix: Turn on account creation (--jit) or invite the person first. Without it, SAML only signs in people who already have an account.

trouble.problem: Groups do not grant access
trouble.fix: Sync is on, no group matched and there is no default role. Add a mapping or set a default role.

faq.q: Does it work with Okta, Entra ID and Keycloak?
faq.a: Those three have step by step setup guides in the SAML documentation, and any standards compliant SAML 2.0 IdP can be imported by metadata.

faq.q: What if the IdP is down?
faq.a: Root users always keep password sign-in. If the root password is lost, reset it on the host with the recover-admin command.

entries.summary: Let Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or any SCIM 2.0 client create, update and deactivate Levelrail accounts and groups with a bearer token.
gets: Users and groups created and updated from the directory, driving roles through the same mappings as SAML.
Immediate session and API token revocation when a user is deactivated.
Audit entries such as scim.user.deactivated with the SCIM token as actor.
entries.ui_path: Settings > Single sign-on (/settings/sso), then open the Directory sync (SCIM) section
cli: levelrail-cli sso scim tokens create okta-provisioning
auth: HTTP bearer token. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored and it is shown once.

permissions.detail: Creating and rotating SCIM tokens needs root.
/Users and /Groups support list, get, create, replace, PATCH and delete. ServiceProviderConfig and ResourceTypes are readable.

entries.endpoint: SCIM base URL: `https://<dashboard>/api/v1/scim/v2`. SCIM only answers over https.
limits: Interim implementation behind the saml-scim beta feature, off by default.
Bulk, sorting and ETags are not supported. Paging allows at most 200 items per page.
The last root user cannot be deactivated or deleted through SCIM; the request answers 409.
Profile email changes at the IdP do not rename the account.

trouble.problem: The IdP gets 404 from the SCIM base URL
trouble.fix: The saml-scim beta feature is off. Turn it on under Settings, Beta features or with APP_EXPERIMENTAL=saml-scim.

trouble.problem: A deprovision request answers 409
trouble.fix: The target is the last root user. Grant root to someone else first.

trouble.problem: Roles do not change when group membership changes
trouble.fix: With no group to role mappings configured SCIM never changes roles. Add mappings under Single sign-on.

faq.q: Do I need SAML as well?
faq.a: No. People can sign in with SAML, OAuth or a password. SCIM only manages accounts and groups.

faq.q: What happens to a deleted user?
faq.a: The account is kept but disabled, so history and ownership stay intact. Creating the same email again restores it.

entries.what: run and back up managed PostgreSQL databases
entries.summary: Create a managed PostgreSQL database with scheduled backups to S3 compatible storage, point-in-time restore and a guarded major upgrade.
gets: A PostgreSQL 16 container with generated settings and its own data volume that survives container recreation.
Connection details and an injectable connection string for apps.
Backups as pg_dump backups, with schedules and retention.
Point-in-time restore through WAL archiving, for Postgres only.
pgvector images through a version such as 17-pgvector.
entries.ui_path: Databases > Create database (engine PostgreSQL)
auth: Credentials are generated by Levelrail and exposed through the connection string.

permissions.detail: A user with write access to databases; public access and deletion are separate decisions in the UI.

entries.endpoint: Engine id `postgres`. Default version `16`. TLS: on by default.
limits: Point-in-time restore and the guarded major upgrade are Postgres only.
A plain Postgres and a pgvector image cannot be swapped with set-version; use major-upgrade, and pgvector back to plain is refused.

trouble.problem: set-version is refused with 409
trouble.fix: A major version change would corrupt the data directory. Use `databases major-upgrade` for Postgres, which dumps and restores.

trouble.problem: Point-in-time restore is not available
trouble.fix: Run `pitr enable <database>` first, and take a base backup. WAL archiving only applies going forward.

trouble.problem: The database is stuck not running
trouble.fix: Check its status condition. The reconciler refuses to start when credentials do not exist yet and reports that as a condition.

faq.q: Can I run pgvector?
faq.a: Yes. Use a version written <major>-pgvector with Postgres 13 or newer, such as 17-pgvector.

faq.q: Which backups can verify themselves?
faq.a: Scheduled backups that succeed are re-verified automatically; manual ones you verify yourself.

entries.what: run and back up managed MySQL databases
entries.summary: Create a managed MySQL database with scheduled backups, a slow query log and restore into a new database.
gets: A MySQL 8 container with generated settings and its own data volume that survives container recreation.
Connection details and an injectable connection string for apps.
Backups as mysqldump backups, with schedules and retention.
Slow query log read from the container, with a 1000 ms default threshold.
entries.ui_path: Databases > Create database (engine MySQL)
auth: Credentials are generated by Levelrail and exposed through the connection string.

permissions.detail: A user with write access to databases; public access and deletion are separate decisions in the UI.

entries.endpoint: Engine id `mysql`. Default version `8`. TLS: off.
limits: Only minor and patch version changes are accepted; a major change is refused with 409.
No in place major upgrade flow: back up and restore as new on the new version.
TLS is not enabled by default.

trouble.problem: set-version returns 409
trouble.fix: MySQL accepts only minor and patch changes. Back up, then `backups restore-as-new` onto the new version.

trouble.problem: Slow query results are empty
trouble.fix: The log reads /var/log/mysql/slow.log and is on from creation. Lower APP_DATABASE_SLOW_QUERY_THRESHOLD_MS if the 1000 ms default hides your queries.

trouble.problem: A backup fails with 507
trouble.fix: The control plane data directory is below APP_MIN_BACKUP_DISK_MB free. Free space there.

faq.q: Can I restore to a different name?
faq.a: Yes. Restore as new creates a new database from a backup, which also serves as the major upgrade path.

faq.q: Is MySQL point-in-time restore available?
faq.a: No. It is Postgres only.

entries.what: deploy from GitHub pushes and pull requests
entries.summary: Connect GitHub once, then point apps at repositories for push deploys, release deploys and per pull request previews.
gets: Push, tag or pull request events that deploy an app or build a preview.
Repository and branch listing plus webhook registration through `use-as-source`.
Webhook history with replay, and PR comments and commit statuses.
entries.ui_path: Settings > GitHub App (/settings/github-app)
auth: A GitHub App created by a manifest flow, or entered by hand. Tokens are short lived and minted per API call.

permissions.detail: Choose which account or organization and which repositories to grant.
Needed for use-as-source to register the webhook. An installation that predates it reports webhook_registered false.

entries.endpoint: Webhook URL per app: `/api/v1/webhooks/github/<app-name>`.
limits: GitHub Enterprise Server works through instance_url.
A private App owned by a personal account cannot be installed on an organization; own it from the organization or make it public.
The manifest flow needs a primary domain set in ingress settings first, otherwise it returns 409.
The connection needs a master key on the control plane; routes return 501 without one.

trouble.problem: Creating the App returns 409
trouble.fix: GitHub needs a reachable callback URL. Set a primary domain in ingress settings, or connect a manually created App.

trouble.problem: The organization is not offered on the install page
trouble.fix: The App is private and owned by a personal account. Make it public in the App's Advanced settings, or create it under the organization.

trouble.problem: use-as-source reports webhook_registered false
trouble.fix: The installation lacks repository_hooks:write. Accept the App's updated permissions, then run use-as-source again.

faq.q: Do I paste a personal access token?
faq.a: No. A GitHub App is a control plane wide credential, and each app gets its own webhook secret.

faq.q: Does disconnecting delete the App on GitHub?
faq.a: No. It removes the connection and secrets from Levelrail only. Remove the App at github.com/settings/apps.
